title: Swaps inside alternative groups

blocks.text: A water utility's scenario diff lists the mains it adds and drops between two runs. Many mains have two options in an alternative group, reline or replace, and at most one option per group is funded. When a diff shows `replace_M4` dropped and `reline_M4` added, the asset managers read it as one decision, "reline main 4 instead of replacing it", and they want the report to say so.

In `swaps.py`, write `pair_swaps(adds, drops, group_of)`. `adds` and `drops` are the diff's two lists; `group_of` maps a project to its alternative group, and a project with no group is absent. Return a dictionary:

items: `"swaps"`: a list of `(dropped, added)` pairs, one per dropped project whose group gained an added project, sorted by the dropped id;
`"adds"` and `"drops"`: what is left of each list once the swapped projects are taken out, sorted.

blocks.text: Because each group keeps $`\sum_{i \in g} \text{started}(i) \le 1`$ in both plans, a group can lose at most one option and gain at most one. Before coding, write down what that row implies about how many swaps one group can produce, and what a project with no group can be paired with. The tests use their own mains.

cases.says: a dropped option and an added option of the same group become one swap, and leave the add and drop lists
a dropped option whose group gained nothing stays a plain drop
projects with no alternative group are never paired, even with each other
swaps are sorted by the dropped option's id

origin.section: A Diff Worth a Few Thousand Is a Near Tie, Not a Decision

concepts: a drop and an add in one alternative group are one swap
